Earlier this year, Apple significantly raised the prices of several products in response to the ongoing global shortage of memory chips. Among them, the iPad Air went from US$599 to US$749, the M5 MacBook Pro from US$1,699 to US$1,999, and Apple TV also rose from US$129 to US$199. The above are just some examples, but the key point is that this round of price hikes was quite staggering.

This naturally raises the question — under the new pricing, will Apple put more effort into product improvements to make consumers feel that "the price hike is worth it"?

Of course, major updates for some of Apple's products are already imminent, with the MacBook Pro and iPad mini being two such examples. However, for models that aren't expected to see major changes in the short term, I really cannot imagine how Apple can make "yesterday's technology" still appealing simply by raising the price — especially considering how abundant the second-hand market options are now.

If you could buy an M4 iPad Air for US$599 (or even as low as US$499) a few months ago, why would you pay US$749 now? This logic becomes even more apparent when applied to higher-priced products.

Some of Apple's products have actually gone a long time without major changes. The iPad Air has barely changed in design or features since 2020, with only chip upgrades and added Apple Pencil Pro support. The entry-level iPad has largely remained the same since 2022, and the iMac has seen no major changes from 2021 to this day.

Do these products really need a complete redesign? Not necessarily. But I think Apple definitely has room to add more attractive upgrades on top of the existing pricing. For example, the iMac could get a miniLED display, the iPad Air could be bumped up to a 120Hz refresh rate, and the entry-level iPad could switch to a fully laminated screen.

Compared to the cost of the price hike, the cost of such upgrades is relatively limited, yet effective in making consumers feel that it's "worth buying". Conversely, Apple could also consider "cutting back a little" to offset the pricing pressure — for instance, the iPhone might once again offer a 128GB storage option.

What are your thoughts on Apple's product lineup after the price hike? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
